words: Late, interested, inconsistent Gospel traditions and willingness to die cannot establish resurrection history, so Craig must substantiate his claimed scholarly consensus and evidentiary inference.
critique: Strongest feature: The reply directly contests Craig’s multiple-source argument and claimed historical consensus, pressing whether late, interested, inconsistent Gospel traditions or martyrdom willingness establish resurrection fact. Principal limitation: Although Stenger mentions surveys and qualified biblical scholars, the excerpt names neither, ends before completing their reported conclusion, and presents no dating, inconsistency, interest, or martyrdom evidence, weakening evidence warrant and calibration. Live burden: Stenger must identify representative scholarship and demonstrate how particular source dates, textual conflicts, authorial interests, or death claims defeat Craig’s inference instead of merely asserting disputed consensus. Locked score: The exact score of 72 fits because responsiveness and burden relevance are stronger, while evidence warrant and calibration remain weaker, limiting an otherwise coherent and reasonably precise reply.
